questions.question: Discuss the classification of carbohydrates, including their functions, types (monosaccharides, disaccharides, oligosaccharides, polysaccharides), and dietary sources.?
questions.solution_html:
• Carbohydrates- Carbohydrates are the most abundant organic molecules in
  • nature and the major functional constituents of living cells. A carbohydrate is
  • a biomolecule consisting of carbon (C), hydrogen (H) and oxygen (O) atoms, usually
  • with a hydrogen–oxygen atom ratio of 2:1 (as in water). Classification
  • Monosaccharides-The word “Monosaccharides” derived from the Greek word
  • “Mono” means Single and “saccharide” means sugar. Monosaccharides are simple
  • sugars. They are sweet in taste. They are soluble in water. They are crystalline in
  • nature. Eg; glucose, fructose, galactose 2. Disaccharides-Disaccharides are produced
  • from the condensation of 2 monosaccharide molecules. Eg; lactose, maltose, sucrose.
questions.final_answer: Option (c) , hydrogen (H) and oxygen (O) atoms, usually

questions.question: Describe the importance and principles of meal planning? END OF THE QUESTION PAPER ***
questions.solution_html:
• Meal planning is defined as a simple process which involves the application of
  • the knowledge of food, nutrient, food habits, likes and dislikes to plan wholesome and
  • attractive meals
  • Importance of meal planning- Meet the nutritional needs of the individuals who will
  • be consuming the food, Plan meal within the food budget, Simplify purchase
  • preparation, and storage of foods, Provide attractive, appetizing meal with no
  • monotony, Save time and money, Minimize the overhead expenditure, i.e fuel
  • electricity, water and labour, Reduce mealtime stress
  • Principles of meal planning: Adequacy, balance, calorie control, nutrient density
  • variety, moderation.
questions.final_answer: variety, moderation
